survivingClaim: Stage A only; nothing about zeros of zeta. For E*(z, rho/2) on PSL_2(Z) the completed Rankin-Selberg function is G(w) = xi(w+beta-1) xi(w+1-beta) xi(w+i gamma) xi(w-i gamma); at xi(rho) = 0 it has exactly one simple pole pair, at w = 2-beta and beta-1 (the other six residues carry xi(rho)). The gamma pole of the even twists is at 1-beta, where the twisted product vanishes because L(0, chi) = 0 for even chi, for every parameter, zero or not. The LRS-type inequality (exponent count ARGUED, reconstructed, not checked against the paper) reduces to beta <= 7/4, which is vacuous. The Eisenstein series at a generic parameter passes every step with the same output (confirmed by me at beta = 0.7 and 0.15). For Borel Eisenstein data of any rank at regular parameters, and for any Hecke eigen-object with the same Satake parameters, pole position minus gamma-pole position equals 1. Device closed as a precise obstruction; DH and T-NR not formulated.
obstruction: Stage A. At xi(rho) = 0 the completed Rankin-Selberg function has one simple pole pair, but at P = 2 - beta; the gamma pole read by the mechanism is at 1 - beta, so pole minus parameter is 1 for every beta. The vanishing forced there is the trivial zero L(0,chi) = 0 of even chi, an identity for every parameter. The inequality reduces to beta <= 7/4 (vacuous; exponent count reconstructed, paper not opened). Same for Borel Eisenstein data of any rank at regular parameters. Open cell without a candidate: non-Borel Hecke eigen-object with parameter rho, entire twists and pole strictly left of 2 - beta.

lesson: Cuspidality enters LRS three times: entire twists, a single Rankin-Selberg pole, and that pole's position P=1 (square-integrability). A zero supplies the single pole but not its position: for Eisenstein data the pole sits at 1 plus the parameter in every rank, and the forced vanishing at the gamma pole is a trivial zero.
